record.original_question: Is the generating function Σ_{n≥0} x^n/n! Σ_{π∈S_n, E(π)=0} 2^{κ(π)} B̄_{κ(π)}(z) equal to e^{2zx/(1-x)}?

evidence.quote: Conjecture 4.2 We have the generating function Σ_{n=0}^∞ x^n/n! Σ_{π∈S_n, E(π)=0} 2^{κ(π)} B̄_{κ(π)}(z) = e^{2zx/(1−x)}.

artifact.self_contained_problem:
For a permutation $\pi \in S_n$ written in disjoint cycle decomposition, let $\kappa(\pi)$ denote the total number of cycles of $\pi$ and let $E(\pi)$ denote the number of cycles of $\pi$ of even length. For an integer $k \geq 0$, let $\bar B_k(z)$ denote the $k$-th Bell (Touchard) polynomial, defined by the exponential generating function
$$\sum_{k\ge 0} \bar B_k(z)\,\frac{t^k}{k!} \;=\; e^{\,z(e^{t}-1)}\,,$$
so that $\bar B_k(z)=\sum_{j=0}^{k} S(k,j)\,z^{j}$, where $S(k,j)$ are the Stirling numbers of the second kind.

Decide whether the following identity of formal power series in $x$ (with coefficients in $\mathbb{Q}[z]$) holds:
$$\sum_{n=0}^{\infty} \frac{x^{n}}{n!} \sum_{\substack{\pi\in S_n\\ E(\pi)=0}} 2^{\kappa(\pi)}\,\bar B_{\kappa(\pi)}(z) \;=\; \exp\!\left(\frac{2zx}{1-x}\right).$$

Here the inner sum is taken over those permutations $\pi$ of $\{1,2,\dots,n\}$ whose cycle decomposition contains no cycle of even length (with the empty permutation in $S_0$ contributing $\bar B_0(z)=1$).
artifact.status_search_result: A direct web search did not return any source explicitly resolving this conjectural identity (involving permutations with only odd-length cycles, weighted by $2^{\kappa(\pi)}\bar B_{\kappa(\pi)}(z)$, summing to $e^{2zx/(1-x)}$). No proof, disproof, or reference to a subsequent resolution was located, so the current status is unclear.
